chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, who said:
“If the thief enters upon you intending your family and your property, then if you are able to preempt him and strike him, then preempt him and strike him.”
And he said: “The thief is one who wages war against Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, so kill him; whatever harm from him touches you is upon me.”

key_terms.أَهْلَكَ: your family; the members of one’s household under threat
key_terms.اللِّصُّ: the thief; the aggressor who unlawfully enters to seize or violate
key_terms.تَبْدُرَهُ: to preempt him; to act before he carries out his assault
key_terms.فَاقْتُلْهُ: kill him; an authorization of lethal force in this context
key_terms.فَمَا مَسَّكَ مِنْهُ: whatever harm from him touches you; any injury suffered from the assailant
key_terms.فَهُوَ عَلَيَّ: it is upon me; responsibility is borne by the Imam عليه السلام
key_terms.مَالَكَ: your property; one’s possessions and wealth being targeted
key_terms.مُحَارِبٌ: one waging war; an aggressor treated as openly hostile to divine and prophetic order

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām say about defending oneself and one’s family from a thief?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning defense against an attacking thief who seeks one's family and property. It characterizes such a thief as a muharib against Allah and His Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, indicating the severity of the offense and the permissibility of forceful self-defense.
